issues.legal_issue: Criminal proceedings may be quashed when a complaint concerning transactions already in civil litigation is initiated after a substantial delay with an ulterior motive to harass the accused.
material_facts: Civil suits seeking specific performance of agreements concerning the same transactions had been filed and were being contested.
The complainant had filed written statements in the civil suits denying execution of the agreements before making the criminal complaint.
The criminal complaint was filed substantially later than the institution of the civil suits and the filing of the written statements.
The Court found that the complaint had been filed with an ulterior motive to harass the accused.
issues.conclusion: The criminal proceedings were manifestly attended with mala fides and fell within the category of cases in which proceedings may be quashed to prevent abuse of process; the FIRs were quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, proceedings may be quashed where they are manifestly attended with mala fides or maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive to wreak vengeance or pursue a private grudge. State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal identifies this as a category warranting quashing, while cautioning that the power should be exercised sparingly and with circumspection.

rule.if: challenge_to_criminal_proceedings and same_transactions_in_civil_suits and complaint_filed_after_civil_defense and complaint_filed_to_harass

predicates.challenge_to_criminal_proceedings: The accused sought to have criminal proceedings set aside.
predicates.same_transactions_in_civil_suits: The complainant and accused were already contesting civil suits concerning the transactions underlying the criminal complaint.
predicates.complaint_filed_after_civil_defense: The complainant filed the criminal complaint substantially after filing a defense in the civil litigation.
predicates.complaint_filed_to_harass: The complaint was initiated with an ulterior motive to harass the accused.
predicates.criminal_proceedings_quashed: The criminal proceedings are set aside.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns criminal proceedings arising from transactions already contested in civil suits, and the complaint followed the civil defense and was filed to harass the accused, the proceedings are set aside.

issues.legal_issue: A Magistrate must not entertain an application seeking a police investigation unless it is supported by a duly sworn affidavit from the applicant.
material_facts: The complainants sought a direction for police investigation through private complaints.
The Magistrate referred the complaints to the police for investigation.
The applications seeking investigation were not supported by sworn affidavits.
The Magistrate did not account for the governing requirements when making the referral, and the High Court did not correct that error.
issues.conclusion: The Magistrate ought not to have entertained the applications under Section 156(3) because they were unsupported by affidavits; the resulting proceedings were quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Priyanka Srivastava v. State of Uttar Pradesh holds that an application under Section 156(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure must be supported by a duly sworn affidavit, and that prior applications under Sections 154(1) and 154(3) should be made and their particulars stated. The affidavit promotes responsibility and deters casual or false applications; in an appropriate case, the Magistrate may verify the truth and veracity of the allegations.

predicates.challenge_to_investigation_referral: The accused challenged proceedings that followed a Magistrate's referral for police investigation.
predicates.application_for_police_investigation: The complainant asked the Magistrate to refer the complaint to police for investigation.
predicates.application_lacked_sworn_affidavit: The application seeking the investigation referral was not supported by a duly sworn affidavit from the applicant.
predicates.application_not_entertained: The Magistrate does not entertain the application seeking the investigation referral.

issues.definition: When an accused challenges an investigation referral sought by an application that lacked a sworn affidavit, the application is not entertained.
